item.title: 'Reverse the downward spiral': Nikki Haley urges US to strengthen ties with India
item.description: Nikki Haley urges the US to strengthen its partnership with India, viewing it as a crucial ally against China's growing influence. She emphasises India's manufacturing capabilities, strategic location, and economic growth as vital assets for countering Beijing. Haley warns against undermining the relationship, advocating for direct talks between Trump and Modi to address trade disputes and shared goals.

item.title: ODNI-shakeup: Trump admin orders major cuts to intelligence office as 40% staff axed
item.description: The Trump administration, under Director Tulsi Gabbard, is implementing significant cuts to the Office of the Director of National Intelligence, reducing its budget and workforce substantially. Gabbard asserts these changes aim to eliminate politicization and restore trust, while critics express concerns about the impact on national security.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: US appeals court backs Trump admin: Halts TPS relief for 60,000 migrants; Nepal, Honduras in focus
item.description: A US federal appeals court has paused a lower court's order. This order had shielded about 60,000 migrants from Honduras, Nicaragua, and Nepal from deportation. The 9th US circuit court's decision supports the Trump administration's plan. The plan is to end Temporary Protected Status for these groups. The next hearing in the case is scheduled for November 18.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘Crazy-communist white hippies’: Chants & boos disrupt JD Vance’s national guard lunch; DC pushback grows
item.description: JD Vance's lunch with National Guard troops faced protests in Washington. Demonstrators opposed the Trump administration's security deployment. Vance dismissed protesters as 'crazy'. He defended the troop presence. He questioned crime data accuracy. Protesters held signs and chanted slogans. Tensions remain high between DC residents and the federal government. The visit highlighted differing views on public safety.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: No Epstein grand jury transcript unsealing: Judge rejects DOJ’s request; testimony called ‘hearsay’
item.description: In a recent ruling, a US judge denied the government's request to unseal grand jury transcripts in the Jeffrey Epstein case, deeming them of limited value compared to the broader case file. Judge Berman highlighted that the testimony was hearsay from an FBI agent with no direct knowledge of the crimes.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Man sets fire, smashes desks at Milan airport: Delays, evacuation follow - Watch
item.description: Chaos erupted at Milan's Malpensa Airport as a man was apprehended after allegedly damaging check-in desks with a hammer and setting fire to Terminal One. The incident, which occurred around 11 am local time, led to evacuations and flight disruptions. An airport employee was injured while intervening. Police are investigating the suspect's motives after he was restrained by authorities.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Doerner Fir on fire: One of world’s tallest trees burns from inside; 50 feet lost, cause unknown
item.description: Oregon firefighters are fighting a fire inside the Doerner Fir. This coastal Douglas Fir is over 325 feet tall. The fire started on Saturday in Coos County. It is burning inside the tree trunk, high above the ground. Helicopter bucket drops have reduced fire activity. Sprinklers are set up at the base. The fire has caused visible damage.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Alaska summit: Putin paid cash to refuel planes, says Rubio; sanctions block banking access
item.description: During a high-stakes meeting in Alaska, President Putin's delegation faced an unusual hurdle, having to pay cash for jet fuel due to US banking sanctions, revealed US Secretary of State Marco Rubio. Despite the sanctions and a proposed ceasefire deal, no formal agreement emerged from the summit with President Trump.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Xi in Tibet: China's president makes rare visit to Lhasa; urges political stability, religious harmony
item.description: President Xi Jinping's rare visit to Lhasa marked Tibet's 60th anniversary as an autonomous region, emphasizing stability and ethnic unity. This visit, coupled with Foreign Minister Wang Yi's trip to India, signals China's strategic interests in the region. Concerns persist over China's governance, hydropower projects, and the Dalai Lama's succession, amidst claims of repression and infrastructure development.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 'I've settled six wars': Trump calls Netanyahu 'war hero'; says he is one too
item.description: Donald Trump praised Benjamin Netanyahu for ordering strikes on Iranian nuclear sites. Trump called Netanyahu a war hero. He also suggested he deserved the same title. These comments followed Israeli airstrikes on Iranian nuclear facilities. The US also deployed bombs against Iran's Fordo facility. Trump claimed to have eased tensions in several global conflicts.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Maga Thaw? Why Elon Musk is shelving third-party dreams - and will back JD Vance instead
item.description: Musk’s involvement in the 2024 election extended far beyond flashy endorsements. His America PAC poured nearly $300 million into the battleground states, leveraging advanced messaging strategies and the reach of X to engineer strategic voter influence. While Trump commanded the stage, Musk controlled the backstage, shaping narrative arcs with precision. That campaign muscle powered by Silicon Valley optics helped catapult JD Vance, then Trump’s running mate, into the vice presidency. Musk’s campaign infrastructure evolved into a potent political tool, forging a bond with Vance that is equal parts ideology and necessity.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: The Urge to Purge: US gives immigration officials discretionary powers to determine if social media posts are 'anti-American'
item.description: Amidst growing concerns, the Trump administration's social media vetting and 'America First' policy are sparking division. Oklahoma plans to screen teachers from liberal states for 'woke' views. Trump criticized museums, including the Smithsonian and the National Museum of African American History and Culture, for focusing on negativity and slavery.
item.dc:creator: Chidanand Rajghatta

item.title: 'Nobel-er' Intentions? Donald Trump wants peace in Ukraine – so he can go to heaven
item.description: President Trump, twice impeached, once convicted, and forever a master of spectacle, wants to end the war in Ukraine because he wants to go to heaven."I want to try and get to heaven, if possible," he said on live television. "I'm hearing I'm not doing well. I'm really at the bottom of the totem pole."With that, the most powerful man on Earth confessed that even he was afraid of the next world. Trump was not playing 4D chess. He was bargaining with God.​
item.dc:creator: Nirmalya Dutta

item.title: Oman’s real estate breaks records: The Arc at Yiti sells most expensive penthouse for over OMR 2 million
item.description: The Arc at The Sustainable City – Yiti has set a national record with the sale of Oman’s most expensive penthouse, exceeding OMR 2 million. This milestone reflects soaring demand for sustainable luxury living. Developed by Diamond Developers and OMRAN, the project aligns with Oman Vision 2040, offering net-zero emissions, smart infrastructure, and a future-ready urban lifestyle.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: UAE weather forecast: 4 days of mixed weather ahead, what residents need to know
item.description: The UAE will experience fluctuating weather from August 21 to 24, with partly to fully cloudy skies, chances of rainfall, mainly in the east and south, and occasional dusty winds reaching up to 45 km/h. Sea conditions will remain slight to moderate. The NCM advises residents to stay updated, especially as temperatures dip slightly and winds intensify during the day.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Prince William and Kate Middleton set sights on Forest Lodge as their long-term base
item.description: Prince William and Princess Kate are reportedly planning a move to Forest Lodge in Windsor Great Park later this year, potentially making it their primary residence even after William ascends the throne. This eight-bedroom Georgian house offers privacy and space, aligning with their children's schooling and a desire for a stable family life amidst royal duties.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: EV revolution: Dubai to get 200 ultra-fast EV chargers, cutting charging times under 30 minutes
item.description: Parkin and charge&go by e& are launching a network of 200 ultra-fast EV chargers across Dubai, significantly reducing charging times to under 30 minutes. This initiative supports Dubai's sustainable transportation goals and aligns with the UAE's green energy objectives. The chargers will be strategically located in residential areas, retail centers, and leisure hubs, enhancing convenience for EV drivers.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk
